bio: Yu Wang is a Bay Area-based Chinese documentary filmmaker and visual journalist.

Growing up between Shanghai, one of the country’s most modern cities, and her family’s hometown, a rural landscape shaped by uneven social development, she is naturally drawn to individuals’ stories, especially those about labor, human rights, and social change. She hopes that through her lens, the stories most in need of being seen can one day reach the people who need to see them most, like the butterfly effect.
She’s also a grip, a Japanese speaker, and a six-year Final Fantasy player.

videos.title: For All Of Us
videos.description: After decades-long fights, California gig workers won the right to form their union for the first time. For All of Us follows the life of Alejandra, a single mother and Uber driver for 12 years, as she joins the movement to form the first-ever rideshare drivers’ union in California.

videos.title: Where Do We Go?
videos.description: As the City of Berkeley moves to shut down the encampment at 8th and Harrison Street, the unhoused people living there are losing the last place they call home. Where Do We Go? follows the residents as they come together to form the Berkeley Homeless Union, using ADA protections and a lawsuit to fight for the survival of their community.

videos.title: Dale, friend of the park
videos.description: Dale, Friend of the Park, is a profile work introducing Dale Risden. Growing up near Joaquin Miller Park in Oakland, his deep memories and emotional bond with the park eventually led him back home. Now, he is dedicated to wildfire prevention work and brings that mission to his neighborhood and to the next generation of youth.

videos.title: Seventeen
videos.description: Seventeen focused on the lives of minor workers in a garment factory in Weifang, documenting how they dropped out of school early and spent days in the small village. The job was passed from generation to generation, but the Z Generation workers started to live-stream on the internet during work, fool their leader, and try to figure out their future path with their dreams.

videos.title: Cross the river
videos.role: Producer/Cinematographer/Editor | Published in the Paper and screened at Shanghai Media Group
videos.description: Cross the River followed Nianxi Chen, the miner who became famous for his poetry. He suffered from pneumoconiosis due to insufficient labor protection in his early years, and was facing his creative transformation with a lack of poetry materials. We travelled with him along the River Luo to record how individual destinies were incorporated into social transformation.

videos.title: A Conversation with Barbecue Owners: Fame and Challenges
videos.role: Independent work | Published in the Paper
videos.description: The overnight popularity Zibo gained on Chinese social media in 2023 drew a huge number of tourists here and exceeded the city’s capacity to accommodate tourists. A conversation with Barbecue Owners documented a visual oral history of three local business owners to discuss how a city coped with sudden popularity and what changes were brought to the local people.

videos.title: Becoming an Idol: 30 Days
videos.role: Director/Cinematographer/Editor | Published in the Paper, the First Prize of Microfilm works in the Wangdao Media Award.
videos.description: Becoming an Idol followed an idol group since their debut. These girls dreamed of standing on the stage, yet they knew deep down that they were not destined to become stars. Caught in this mixed feeling, they kept practicing, quarreling, learning how to maintain their fans, and cherishing every chance they got to perform as underground idols: performers outside the mainstream entertainment industry.

videos.title: Just for Dinner
videos.role: Director of Photograph| Official Selection, the 8th 48filMarathon International Film Festival
videos.description:
From the ingredients they buy to the flavors they prefer, from their cooking habits to their daily routines, the two young roommates couldn’t be more different. Yet over one shared meal after another, their relationship quietly begins to shift, until the very last dinner.

- So what's our relationship now?

- Just for Dinner.
